chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), 'Where should the strangers perform ablution?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They should avoid the banks of the rivers, the thoroughfares, under the fruit-bearing trees, and the places of curse.' So it was said to him, 'And where are the places of the curse?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The doors of the houses.'
ai.seo_question: Where should one perform ablution according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the etiquette of urination, emphasizing adab (manners) by avoiding places where people frequently pass or enter, such as thoroughfares, riverbanks, and under fruit trees. Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn specifically identifies 'doors of houses' as 'places of curse' (mawadi' al-la'nah), a concept rooted in Shia jurisprudence linking the disruption of privacy and the exposure of one's private parts to divine displeasure. The guidance reflects a broader Islamic principle of maintaining cleanliness and modesty in communal spaces.
